meta.name: trustline curated dependency advisories (incident-anchored)
meta.source: Anchored to this incident's entry point and to a well-known Web3 supply-chain compromise. This is a deliberately small, curated set (not a general npm-audit): every entry maps to a documented dApp-layer attack.
meta.matching: Compares the version declared in package.json (dependencies, devDependencies, optionalDependencies, peerDependencies) against the affected version list, after stripping leading range operators. Lockfile-aware resolution of ranges is future work.

advisories.title: React2Shell: unauthenticated RCE in React Server Components (Flight payload deserialization)
advisories.fix: Upgrade react-server-dom-* past the affected versions (19.1.2 / 19.2.1 or later) and redeploy.
advisories.chain: This is the exact entry point of this incident: one crafted request runs code on the Node server with no authentication, handing over the whole process and letting every downstream config mistake turn into full compromise.

advisories.title: Malicious @ledgerhq/connect-kit versions ship a wallet drainer (2023 supply-chain compromise)
advisories.fix: Upgrade @ledgerhq/connect-kit to 1.1.8 or later and audit any wallet interactions that loaded the affected version.
advisories.chain: A compromised npm account pushed drainer code into this dependency, so every dApp that loaded it drained visitors' wallets straight from the front end, no contract bug required.
